misconceptions.believed: That decay meant 'pull the value toward the middle', full stop. That is what the trajectory's own sentence describes -- mastery drifts back toward the middle over weeks -- and it is what I set out to implement.
misconceptions.revealed_by: Q90, which I had written at the end of W5 and which forced the question before any code existed. A tag decaying from 0.2 toward 0.5 spends weeks below DRILL_BELOW on the way, so a player who went away would be drilled on their return; and a strong player decaying down into the drill band would be drilled too.
misconceptions.corrected_to: Decay has to reach `confident`, not only `value`. A stale estimate should make the player unmeasured, and the model already has a word for that. With the observation count eroding at the same half-life, six weeks away drops a tag out of confidence and the policy falls back to the standard variant -- which is what 're-assess returning players' actually means, as opposed to 'give them a slightly different number'.
misconceptions.generalisable_lesson: A spec sentence can be complete about what moves and silent about what that means downstream. 'Drifts back toward the middle' is accurate and would have produced a worse game, because the trajectory phrased the mechanism and I was responsible for the consequence. The check that worked was asking what each other part of the system would do with the decayed value, one at a time. It also argues for recording an open question the moment you notice it: this one cost five minutes as a note in S029 and would have cost a session as a bug report.

decisions.decision: Decay erodes the observation count as well as the value
alternatives: Decay the value only, as the trajectory's sentence describes
decisions.rationale: Otherwise a returning player reads as measured-and-mediocre rather than unmeasured, and gets drilled for having been away. Confidence is already the model's word for 'we do not know yet'.

decisions.decision: Decay is a read-time view, never written to the profile
decisions.rationale: The stored profile should stay a record of what was measured rather than one that rots on disk. Writing on load would also reset the clock it is measured against.

decisions.decision: observe decays before applying new evidence, and writes that back
alternatives: Observe from the stored value and let the view handle it
decisions.rationale: At that moment the decay is not an interpretation -- a new run has superseded the old reading. Without it a two-month absence still moves from the August rating.

alternatives: 7 days, too eager -- a fortnight off would erase you
90 days, too slow to re-assess anyone
decisions.rationale: Puts a 90% estimate at 70% after a month and out of confidence after six weeks, roughly the interval over which a person's Python actually changes. Unplaytested and labelled as such.

decisions.decision: A missing, mangled or naive timestamp decays nothing
alternatives: Treat an unparseable stamp as ancient
decisions.rationale: The profile is a file the player is invited to edit, and entries written before W1 have no stamp at all. Refusing to decay costs a re-assessment; guessing 'ancient' silently erases a profile.

handoff.state: T4 W1-W6 LANDED. Mastery is measured per tag, decays with a three-week half-life in both value and confidence, drives difficulty with a reason attached, and offers a drill when the player is measurably weak and the evidence is fresh. Exit criteria 1, 2, 4 and 5 verified; 3 verified for the two simulated players who can fail (Q89). 1211 tests green unpinned, 1187 pinned, verify clean on 54 reference runs.

open_questions.answer: Decay erodes the observation count as well as the value, so a stale estimate stops being confident. Staleness therefore makes a player unmeasured rather than weak, and no drill is offered: they are re-assessed by playing a standard variant (D192).

open_questions.question: Nothing tells the player their mastery decayed. A returning player sees a standard variant with the reason 'nothing measured yet', which is true of the decayed model and misleading about their history -- they did play, it just aged out. Should the explanation distinguish 'never measured' from 'measured, but a while ago'?
